briefings.title: AI at the Edge: S3 E2
briefings.tldr: Liquid AI is pioneering a new class of "Liquid Foundation Models" (LFMs) that are two orders of magnitude smaller than traditional cloud-based models, enabling high-performance, proactive AI agents to run entirely offline on edge devices like AI PCs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Liquid AI is pioneering a new class of "Liquid Foundation Models" (LFMs) that are two orders of magnitude smaller than traditional cloud-based models, enabling high-performance, proactive AI agents to run entirely offline on edge devices like AI PCs.

## Architectural Innovation: Liquid Neural Networks (LNNs)
* **Brain-Inspired Computation:** Liquid AI moved away from standard transformer architectures to create LNNs based on how neurons exchange information in nature.
    * **Efficiency Gains:** The company aims to shrink models from the trillion-parameter regime used in the cloud to a 100M to 10B parameter range without sacrificing quality.
    * **Alternative Primitives:** Unlike transformers that rely almost exclusively on matrix multiplication, LFMs explore diverse mathematical operators to optimize for memory and speed.
* **Hardware-in-the-Loop Design:** The team uses a meta-AI system to search for the most efficient computational graph for a specific processor (CPU, NPU, or GPU).
    * **Performance Metrics:** This approach targets a memory footprint as small as 1GB while achieving latencies as low as 20 milliseconds for large language model (LLM) tasks.

## The Shift to Proactive Edge AI
* **Reactive vs. Proactive Agents:** Current AI often waits for a prompt (reactive); Liquid AI enables "proactive agents" that run continuously in the background to perform tasks on a user’s behalf.
* **On-Device Advantages:**
    * **Privacy and Security:** By running models locally on Ryzen AI PCs, users can process sensitive data (financials, health records, or secret projects) in "air-gapped" environments.
    * **Latency and Reliability:** Local execution eliminates the need for an internet connection and avoids the latency spikes of cloud-based APIs.
    * **Multimodality:** LFMs are designed to handle vision, text, and audio—noting that low latency is particularly critical for natural audio interactions.

## Power Efficiency and Sustainability
* **NPU Optimization:** Liquid AI works closely with AMD to optimize workloads for Neural Processing Units (NPUs), which provide high-compute throughput (50-60 TOPs) at significantly lower power than traditional chips.
* **Sustainability:** By "juicing out" maximum intelligence per watt at the algorithmic level, Liquid AI addresses the global energy crisis created by the massive power demands of traditional generative AI data centers.
* **Societal Impact:** Mark Papermaster highlights that driving down the cost and power requirements of AI is a form of "democratization," making advanced intelligence accessible to regions or industries without massive infrastructure.

## Ecosystem and the Future of Co-Design
* **Open Source Commitment:** Liquid AI releases its models as "open weights," reporting over 1 million downloads per week as of early 2024.
* **Market Scale:** Ramin Hasani estimates that out of the 35 billion processors manufactured annually, approximately 2 billion (across phones, laptops, and cars) are currently capable of hosting LFMs.
* **Hardware-Software Co-Design:** The ultimate vision is a "holistic design" where the foundation model layer is so deeply integrated into the silicon that the chip itself is inherently "agent-aware."

> "We are talking about shrinking down the size of intelligence to the point, without sacrificing quality, that you can deliver the same quality of those cloud models on the device... that required a change of model architecture and thinking about other primitives of computations." — **Ramin Hasani**

> "If an AI system can run in the background... you can enable something I call proactive agents. They can perform a job that you actually give to the system and they can really be an agent on your behalf—an army of assistants." — **Ramin Hasani**

> "Taking the type of capabilities and agentic processing that today can only be run in the cloud, right into PCs and other very, very efficient devices... it's basically a democratization, making AI available to the masses." — **Mark Papermaster**

briefings.title: Exclusive: ECB President Lagarde Speaks to Bloomberg
briefings.tldr: ECB President Christine Lagarde characterizes the current European economy as sitting between "baseline" and "adverse" scenarios due to significant energy shocks, asserting that the ECB will remain agile and data-dependent rather than committed to a pre-defined rate path.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** ECB President Christine Lagarde characterizes the current European economy as sitting between "baseline" and "adverse" scenarios due to significant energy shocks, asserting that the ECB will remain agile and data-dependent rather than committed to a pre-defined rate path.

## Economic Outlook and Forecasting Scenarios
* **Current Projections:** The ECB has revised its growth forecast down to 0.9% and its inflation forecast to 2.6%.
* **Scenario Modeling:** Lagarde identifies three tiers for the economy: Baseline, Adverse, and Severe. 
    * **Current Status:** The Eurozone is currently positioned between the baseline and the adverse scenario, largely dictated by fluctuating oil and gas prices.
* **Economic Fragility:** Lagarde notes that while recovery was underway post-pandemic, the war-induced energy shock created massive fragmentation. She identifies Asia as the "first victim" in terms of economic losses, though Europe faces significant direct impacts.
* **The "Schizophrenic" Mandate:** Central bankers must perform the dual task of focusing on medium-term price stability while monitoring highly volatile daily data, such as ship movements and spot oil prices.

## Monetary Policy and Strategy
* **Data Dependency:** Lagarde emphasizes that the ECB is not currently "predicating" a specific direction for interest rates. Any policy moves will be determined by whether incoming data suggests shocks are "short-lived/see-through" or "long-lasting."
* **Decision Framework:** The Governing Council is watching for "secondary effects" that could de-anchor inflation expectations. If inflation peaks higher and persists, "decisive" action will be taken.
* **Coordination with Fiscal Policy:** Lagarde urges political leaders to ensure fiscal support is "Targeted, Temporary, Transparent, and Tailored" (the T-T-T-T framework) to avoid working against monetary price stability.
* **Commitment to Target:** Despite various scenarios reaching up to 4% inflation, Lagarde insists the ECB’s "compass" remains a firm 2% medium-term target.

## Geopolitical Risks and Energy Infrastructure
* **The Strait of Hormuz:** Identified as the ultimate "worst-case scenario" for global growth. A closure would block 20% of the world’s oil and gas, as well as critical ingredients for fertilizers and microchips.
* **Recovery Timelines:** 
    * **Shipping/Distribution:** Experts suggest a 2-3 month window to resume regular shipping conditions following a truce.
    * **Refineries:** Infrastructure damage (specifically citing facilities in Qatar and Saudi Arabia) could take years, not months, to repair.
* **Market Dichotomy:** Lagarde warns of a "dichotomy" in markets between those acting as if it is "business as usual" and the reality of a significant, long-lasting shock to supply chains and food prices.

## Structural Threats: AI and Political Shifts
* **Artificial Intelligence:** Lagarde identifies AI as a "big issue" that concerns her more than immediate market fluctuations.
    * **Social Impact:** She questions the long-term effects on productivity, mass unemployment, and the "fiscal equilibrium" required for reskilling workers.
    * **Governance Gap:** She notes a lack of a global governance framework to manage the risks of AI falling into the "wrong hands."
* **Political Change in Hungary:** Lagarde welcomed the victory of Péter Magyar, noting his two-thirds majority could remove obstacles to growth. 
    * **Euro Adoption:** She noted Magyar’s interest in Hungary joining the Eurozone, describing it as the "natural path," though she cautioned that the convergence process takes years of judicial and legal reform.
* **Leadership Continuity:** Responding to rumors about her tenure, Lagarde stated, "The captain does not leave the ship" during times of major disruption.

***

> "We central bankers are left with defining the baseline... and because this information that we have is constantly changing and we have a high degree of unpredictability and uncertainty, we have to work on scenarios." — **Christine Lagarde**

> "I take the see-through story into account, but this is not something that you can actually explain to the fisherman who cannot go at sea because he cannot pay for his petrol." — **Christine Lagarde**

> "When there are big clouds on the horizon, the captain does not leave the ship. And this captain is not going to leave the ship." — **Christine Lagarde**

briefings.title: Hans Ulrich Obrist: What business can learn from the art world | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: The most effective leaders act as "junction makers," fostering innovation by creating unexpected connections between disciplines, listening deeply to practitioners, and embracing serendipity over rigid master plans.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The most effective leaders act as "junction makers," fostering innovation by creating unexpected connections between disciplines, listening deeply to practitioners, and embracing serendipity over rigid master plans.

## The Curator as "Junction Maker" and Enabler
* **Defining the Role:** Hans Ulrich Obrist describes curation not as gatekeeping, but as being a "junction maker"—creating situations and unexpected connections between people, ideas, and artworks.
* **The Power of Listening:** Creativity begins with listening rather than imposing a framework.
    * **Artist Advocacy:** Obrist views his role as an "enabler" who helps artists realize dreams that the traditional art world structure might otherwise prohibit.
    * **The Studio Visit:** Obrist has conducted daily studio visits since 1986, emphasizing that the best insights come from long-term, direct engagement with creators.
* **The "Unrealized Project" Inquiry:** A core part of Obrist’s methodology is asking every collaborator about their unrealized projects.
    * **Categories of Failure:** Projects often remain unrealized because they are too big, too time-intensive, censored, or "self-censored" (ideas the creator didn't dare to try).
    * **Untapped Potential:** These "dreams" often sit outside an artist's daily routine and represent their most innovative thinking.

## Innovation Through Multisensory and Digital Experiences
* **Extending Engagement:** To move beyond the "few seconds" visitors typically spend in front of an artwork, the Serpentine creates multisensory environments.
    * **Example:** A Peter Doig exhibition transformed a gallery into a "listening space," encouraging visitors to stay for hours and return repeatedly.
* **Technology as a Lead Medium:** The Serpentine established a dedicated technology department to produce "Future Art Ecosystems."
    * **Gaming and Scale:** A collaboration with *Fortnite* for a KAWS exhibition attracted 150 million virtual visitors in two weeks, successfully bringing a younger generation into the physical gallery.
    * **Ethical AI:** Artists like Holly Herndon and Refik Anadol are used to make "invisible" AI datasets visible and audible, demonstrating how data can be sourced and utilized ethically.
* **Bridging Disciplines:** The Serpentine Pavilion project (now in its 26th year) invites international architects who have never built in the UK to create temporary structures, blending the discourses of art and architecture.

## Long-Term Thinking vs. Short-Termism
* **Continuous Evolution:** Obrist argues against the "short-termist deadlines" of the modern world.
    * **The "do it" Project:** An exhibition based on artist-written instructions that has been evolving and learning for 33 years.
    * **Institutional Re-invention:** The Serpentine adds new departments (e.g., Ecology, Technology) to its organizational "organigram" to stay relevant to societal shifts.
* **Mondialité:** Following the philosophy of Édouard Glissant, Obrist advocates for "mondialité"—a global dialogue that resists the homogenizing forces of globalization while remaining deeply anchored in local culture.
* **The Polyphony of Centers:** The art world has moved from a single center (Paris or New York) to a "polyphony" of global hubs, fueled by private foundations and artist-run initiatives.

## Business Lessons from the Art World
* **The Art of the Pivot:** Artists excel at navigating the "unknowable" and pivoting when faced with uncertainty—skills that are increasingly critical for modern CEOs.
* **Artists in the Boardroom:** Obrist advocates for "Artist Placement Groups," suggesting that every corporation or government entity should have an artist-in-residence or an artist on the board to challenge traditional thinking.
* **Extreme Productivity and Rituals:** Obrist shares his unconventional methods for managing a global workload:
    * **The Night Producer:** He employs a "night assistant" to handle correspondence and editing while he sleeps, ensuring a 24-hour productive cycle.
    * **The Brutally Early Club:** A ritual started in London to hold improvised meetings at 6:30 AM to bypass the rigid scheduling of the business world.

## Notable Quotes
> "Basically what you're doing is you're a junction maker. You create unexpected connections... using the exhibition as a kind of a medium to create experiences." — **Hans Ulrich Obrist** (quoting J.G. Ballard)

> "The way artists work with the unknowable, the way artists work also with questions, often more than with answers, is something I think which can be very relevant today [for business]." — **Hans Ulrich Obrist**

> "We live in a world which is increasingly polarized and separated... I think it's super important that we have situations where we can bring people together. And I think that's what exhibitions can do." — **Hans Ulrich Obrist**

> "I think that's what the best artists do. They kind of negotiate ways of working which are enabling a global dialogue but at the same time are deeply locally anchored." — **Hans Ulrich Obrist**

briefings.title: He Studied $6.4 Trillion Worth of Founders. Here's What They Shared | Mark Macleod | Traction
briefings.tldr: The primary currency of leadership is energy, not hours worked; startups ultimately fail when founders run out of energy, making personal physical, mental, and spiritual health a strategic business imperative rather than a luxury.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The primary currency of leadership is energy, not hours worked; startups ultimately fail when founders run out of energy, making personal physical, mental, and spiritual health a strategic business imperative rather than a luxury.

## The Trillion-Dollar Correlation: Health as a Scaling Strategy
Mark MacLeod’s study of 11 founders (including Tobi Lütke, Jeff Bezos, and Mark Zuckerberg) who built a combined $6.4 trillion in value revealed a consistent pattern: elite performance is tied to rigorous personal maintenance.

*   **Physicality as Strategy:** High-performing CEOs often prioritize physical health as they scale. Examples include Jeff Bezos’s physical transformation and Brian Chesky’s background in competitive bodybuilding.
*   **The "Deadlift ETF":** MacLeod notes an informal study showing that stocks of CEOs who lift weights (e.g., Zuckerberg, Bezos) outperformed the S&P 500 by 2.5x over four years.
*   **The Zone of Genius:** Successful founders like Tobi Lütke (Shopify) protect their energy by delegating tasks that drain them (e.g., Wall Street relations) to partners like Harley Finkelstein, allowing the CEO to stay in their "zone of genius" (product and technology).

## The "Limitless" Leadership Philosophy
The "Limitless" framework rejects "hustle porn" and the narrative of "sleep when I’m dead," arguing that these are the primary drivers of startup failure.

*   **Nervous System as Operating System:** A founder’s internal state dictates company culture. If a founder is "fried," they will inevitably build a "fried" and reactive culture.
*   **The Three Pillars of Energy:**
    *   **Physical:** Prioritizing sleep (the #1 performance hack), real food, and weightlifting (especially for those over 40).
    *   **Mental:** Cultivating "presence" to avoid "time traveling"—the act of simultaneously reliving past mistakes and fearing future ones.
    *   **Spiritual:** Using practices like Kundalini yoga or meditation to tap into intuition and "flow," which MacLeod describes as "spirit is infinite potential."
*   **Acknowledging Limits:** Paradoxically, the path to being limitless begins with acknowledging physical and mental boundaries to avoid burnout.

## Operational Excellence: CEO Altitude and Friction
As a company scales, the CEO's role must shift from "doing" to "clearing the path."

*   **The Three Core CEO Tasks:** Citing Fred Wilson (Union Square Ventures), MacLeod defines the CEO role at scale as:
    1. Communicating the vision/mission.
    2. Building the strongest possible senior leadership team.
    3. Ensuring the company never runs out of money.
*   **Removing Friction:** The CEO should act like "good cholesterol" (HDL), moving through the company to identify and remove friction in products, processes, and teams.
*   **The Dashboard Approach:** Founders should track biomarkers (HRV, sleep scores, blood glucose, and visceral fat) with the same rigor they apply to SaaS KPIs. Changes in these metrics often predict business failures months in advance.

## Integrating Personal and Professional Longevity
Sustainable leadership requires intentionality in personal relationships and the "witness state."

*   **Work-Life Integration:** Excellence is never "balanced" (e.g., LeBron James is not "balanced"). Instead of seeking balance, founders should seek "presence"—being 100% home when they are home.
*   **Marriage Meetings:** MacLeod recommends a structured, weekly "marriage meeting" agenda:
    *   **Gratitude:** Acknowledging what you noticed in your partner.
    *   **Tasks/Chores:** Managing the "operations" of the household.
    *   **Issue Resolution:** A safe forum for addressing conflicts before they metastasize.
*   **Values Alignment:** Conflict often arises not from a lack of love, but from misaligned "operating systems" (e.g., one partner valuing high-agency/risk while the other values stability).

## Notable Quotes
> "Startups die when founders run out of energy. The number one reason why people come to me looking to exit is because they are burnt out." — **Mark MacLeod**

> "Your nervous system is your company operating system. If you're fried, you're gonna build a fried culture." — **Mark MacLeod**

> "The healthy person has a hundred priorities. The sick person has one priority, which is to be healthy. When you're sick, you realize that nothing else matters." — **Mark MacLeod**

> "Pain equals suffering times resistance. There will be suffering in life... whether you experience pain is only a function of whether you resist that suffering." — **Mark MacLeod**

briefings.title: How He Wrote the Biggest Sci-Fi Movie of the Year
briefings.tldr: Science fiction author Andy Weir builds his "hard" sci-fi worlds through rigorous scientific derivation, using complex spreadsheets to ensure fictional elements—like alien biology and interstellar fuel—adhere to the laws of physics or logical "wrong math."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Science fiction author Andy Weir builds his "hard" sci-fi worlds through rigorous scientific derivation, using complex spreadsheets to ensure fictional elements—like alien biology and interstellar fuel—adhere to the laws of physics or logical "wrong math."

## The Mechanics of "Hard" World-Building
* **Scientific Derivation:** Weir does not arbitrarily choose plot points; he derives them from math. For *Project Hail Mary*, he calculated the exact temperature required for the fictional "Astrophage" to generate neutrinos (96.415°C) based on particle velocity and mass-energy.
* **The "Wrong Math" Spreadsheet:** To maintain internal consistency, Weir created a spreadsheet specifically for "wrong math." This calculated how the alien species (the Eridians) would have over-fueled their ships because they lacked a discovery of relativity and relied on Newtonian physics.
* **Special Relativity as a Narrative Limit:** The maximum distance for the Astrophage infection (eight light-years) was derived by calculating how long the organism could survive before radiating away its heat energy, adjusted for its own inertial reference frame.

## Designing Rocky: Logic-Driven Alien Biology
* **Environmental Constraints:** Weir started with the exoplanet 40 Eridani A b. Because the planet is close to its star (a 46-day year), he deduced it needed a thick atmosphere and a massive magnetic field to keep liquid water at 200°C without boiling away.
* **Atmospheric Physics:** 
    * **Composition:** He chose an ammonia atmosphere because ammonia is a heavy molecule that is harder for solar winds to strip away from a gravity well.
    * **Planetary Shape:** Due to its 6-hour rotation and proximity to the Roche limit, Weir calculated the planet would be significantly oblong, resulting in different gravity measurements at the poles versus the equator.
* **Evolutionary Outcomes:** 
    * **Echolocation:** Because no light reaches the surface through the thick atmosphere, the aliens evolved echolocation so precise it functions like vision. 
    * **Inorganic Construction:** Eridians are described as being like a "walking beehive," where internal worker cells build a mostly inorganic carapace, resulting in pentagonal symmetry.
    * **Internalized Biosphere:** Since the atmosphere contains no oxygen, the aliens have an internalized system where they consume food to maintain a biological "internal biosphere" rather than exchanging gases with the environment.

## Collaborative Case Study: Detecting Intelligent Life
* **Energy Signatures:** When brainstorming a new story with Cleo Abram, Weir suggested looking for "energy absorption." A dead planet reflects/emits all radiation it receives; a living planet stores it in chemical bonds (plants/algae), creating a measurable deficit in radiation.
* **The "Steve’s World" Scenario:** In their real-time story collaboration, they imagined an amateur astronomer detecting a sudden electromagnetic burst from a planet (not a star).
    * **Technosignatures:** This would prompt a search for CFCs or pollution—gases that do not occur via natural processes—indicating an industrial civilization.
* **The "Swords to Plowshares" Greeting:** To signal back to a civilization 20 light-years away, Weir suggested detonating a sequence of nuclear bombs in deep space. 
    * **Visibility:** By moving the bombs far from the Sun (e.g., near Saturn or Neptune), the contrast against the dark background of space would make the signal visible to distant telescopes.

## The Role of Optimism and Public Feedback
* **Crowdsourced Fact-Checking:** *The Martian* was originally published chapter-by-chapter online. Readers flagged errors, such as Weir forgetting that hydrogen and oxygen would mix evenly in the "Hab" rather than separating by weight.
* **Narrative Optimism:** Weir avoids dystopias, focusing instead on "good people solving hard problems." He notes that while the news reports on misery, it is only "news" because the norm is actually humans helping one another.
* **The Purpose of Sci-Fi:** For Weir, the ultimate goal is not just education but entertainment. He aims for the "that was cool" feeling that inspired him as a child.

## Notable Quotes

> "The reason you're seeing all this bad stuff on the news is because bad stuff is newsworthy... The kind of compassion and empathy and selflessness that humans have is so ordinary that it's not newsworthy." — **Andy Weir**

> "I wanted my alien in my hard sci-fi book to be really alien. You can't—I wanted our environment to be completely incompatible with theirs." — **Andy Weir**

> "The radiation [the planet] is absorbing is going into the form of life... A dead planet, like Mercury, will be emitting exactly as much radiation as it is absorbing from the sun." — **Andy Weir**

> "I just want them to have a good time. And when they put the book away I want them to think 'that was cool.' That’s all I’m shooting for." — **Andy Weir**

briefings.title: IMF Chief To Unveil Global Policy Agenda Live
briefings.tldr: The global economy faces a "shock upon shock" scenario driven by conflict in the Middle East, with growth projections slowing to 3.1% (and potentially 2% in adverse cases) as public debt is on track to reach post-WWII levels by 2029.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The global economy faces a "shock upon shock" scenario driven by conflict in the Middle East, with growth projections slowing to 3.1% (and potentially 2% in adverse cases) as public debt is on track to reach post-WWII levels by 2029. Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva urges member nations to prioritize macroeconomic stability, avoid unargeted subsidies, and implement structural reforms to build resilience against a 21st-century landscape of frequent disruption.

## Global Economic Outlook and Risks
*   **Revised Growth Projections:** Global growth is slowing from 3.4% last year to a projected 3.1% in 2026.
    *   **Adverse Scenario:** If the Middle East conflict persists and oil prices remain high, growth could drop to 2%.
*   **Inflationary Pressures:** While long-term inflation expectations remain anchored, short-term projections for 2026 have been upgraded due to supply chain disruptions. 
    *   **Commodity Spillovers:** Significant concern regarding fertilizer prices (which have doubled in some regions), which threatens global food security.
*   **Supply Chain Disruptions:** Georgieva described the current crisis as a "20th-century type of shock in the 21st century."
    *   **Logistics Lag:** Tankers are slow-moving vessels; a disruption in the Strait of Hormuz takes roughly 40 days to impact distant markets like Fiji, meaning the full effect of recent events has yet to be felt.
    *   **Energy Intensity:** Shortages are appearing in Asia for oil, gas, naphtha, and helium.

## Strategic Policy Guidance
*   **Monetary Policy:** Georgieva advises a "look before you leap" approach.
    *   **Wait and See:** Countries with high credibility and anchored expectations should pause before raising rates further. 
    *   **Early Action:** Central banks lacking credibility may need to send stronger signals to protect price stability.
*   **Fiscal Discipline:** Global public debt is projected to breach 100% of GDP by 2029. 
    *   **Sustainability vs. Protection:** Policymakers must balance fiscal health with protecting the most vulnerable. 
    *   **Warning Against Unargeted Measures:** The IMF strongly discourages broad-based tax cuts, export controls, and energy subsidies, noting they "prolong the pain" of high prices.
*   **Structural Reform:** Governments are urged to lift productivity through reforms now rather than waiting for shocks to pass. "A strong economy is the best buffer."

## Regional Impacts and Vulnerabilities
*   **MENA Region:** Facing the most severe impact, with growth projections downgraded by 2.3% to a total of 1.4% for 2026. Five out of eight regional oil producers are expected to see negative growth.
*   **Sub-Saharan Africa:** Highly vulnerable due to import dependency and limited fiscal space. The IMF is seeing a surge in demand for programs in this region to address fuel shortages and debt.
*   **Asia-Pacific:** While India remains a "bright spot" with growth twice the global average, the broader region is struggling with energy import dependency. 
    *   **China:** Projections were slightly downgraded (4.5% to 4.4%), but the IMF sees potential if China successfully shifts its model toward domestic consumption.
*   **Climate Vulnerability:** Small island states like Jamaica are facing "repetitive" shocks. The IMF advocates for regional insurance pooling and building "climate-sensitive" infrastructure.

## The IMF’s "Firefighter" Role
*   **Financial Support:** The IMF anticipates near-term demand for financial support to range between $20 billion and $50 billion.
*   **Active Programs:** Currently managing 39 programs, with at least a dozen new requests pending, primarily from African nations.
*   **Toolbox Adaptation:** The IMF is conducting comprehensive reviews of program design, conditionality, and surveillance to sharpen policy advice.
*   **Debt Resolution:** Ongoing work through the Global Sovereign Debt Roundtable aims to address the dangerously high levels of public debt globally.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "What is different this time in comparison to COVID is the cumulative impact of shock upon shock. It has pushed debt to dangerously high levels. Global public debt is on track to breach 100% of GDP in 2029, a level not seen since the aftermath of World War II." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

> "My advice: look before you leap on monetary policy. For countries where monetary policy was well calibrated before the shock and expectations remain anchored, wait and see is the right approach." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

> "In fact, what we have is a 20th-century type of shock—slower-moving shock—in the 21st century... A tanker is a slow-moving vessel. It would take 40 days to get all the way to Fiji." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

> "The most important thing we do for our members is to help them help themselves—to have strong policies during good times to build buffers so during bad times they can protect their people." — **Kristalina Georgieva**

briefings.title: Iran War: Trump Says End to War in Sight, Spurring Market Rally | The Opening Trade 4/15/2026
briefings.tldr: Global markets are rallying on signals from President Trump that the war with Iran may be nearing an end, with investors increasingly prioritizing the "AI boom" and resilient US consumer data over the ongoing shipping crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Global markets are rallying on signals from President Trump that the war with Iran may be nearing an end, with investors increasingly prioritizing the "AI boom" and resilient US consumer data over the ongoing shipping crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

## Geopolitical Outlook & Market Reaction
*   **War De-escalation:** Market optimism is growing as President Trump indicates a potential wind-down of the conflict with Iran, shifting the narrative toward a post-war economic recovery.
*   **Asset Performance:** Major indices, including the S&P 500 and various Asian exchanges (CSI 300, Singapore), have returned to pre-war levels. 
*   **Treasury Positioning:** Markets are heavily positioning for a drop in 10-year yields to the 4%–4.2% range, suggesting that fears of war-driven inflation are being replaced by growth optimism.
*   **Currency Shifts:** The US dollar has surrendered most of its "war gains" as the narrative shifts. However, Deutsche Bank notes that the US consumer may face higher relative gas prices compared to regions with more controlled pump prices.

## Energy Crisis & The Strait of Hormuz
*   **Ongoing Blockade:** Despite market optimism, the Strait of Hormuz remains officially closed due to blockades. Current traffic is described as a "fraction" of the normal 130 vessels per day.
*   **Supply Shortages:** Experts warn that global shortages are building the longer the blockade persists, even if "worst-case" scenarios have not fully materialized yet due to lags in the supply chain.
*   **Testing the Blockade:** 
    *   Iran is reportedly considering a short-term pause in exports to avoid direct military tests of the blockade.
    *   The *Agios Fanourios I* is currently testing the Iranian reaction by heading to Basra to load Iraqi crude for Vietnam; the Trump administration has permitted the move as it is not an Iranian-focused vessel.

## Corporate Earnings: Tech vs. Luxury
*   **Semiconductors & AI:** The tech sector remains the primary engine of market growth, with Guy Johnson noting the current market is essentially a battle of "Strait of Hormuz vs. AI."
    *   **ASML:** Shares surged on positive full-year sales guidance and increased guidance. The company reports being "sold out" and supply-constrained, though Q2 outlook remains cautious. 
*   **Luxury Sector Disruption:** Luxury brands are seeing an indirect hit from the conflict due to tourism disruption.
    *   **Hermes:** Q1 sales grew 5.6% but missed estimates. Markets like the UK, Italy, and Thailand were negatively impacted by a decline in Middle Eastern tourism.
    *   **Kering:** Continuing to struggle with the turnaround of the Gucci brand, though non-Gucci businesses showed some resilience.

## Banking & Macro Indicators
*   **US Bank Resilience:** Recent earnings from JP Morgan, Wells Fargo, Citi, and BlackRock show a divided stock reaction but a consistent theme of high profitability from market turbulence.
*   **"Nice Volatility":** Bank leaders suggest that current market swings have provided profitable trading conditions without the "gappy" instability seen in previous crises.
*   **Upcoming Catalysts:** 
    *   **IMF Spring Meetings:** Ongoing discussions in Washington D.C.
    *   **Central Bank Speakers:** Key commentary expected from the BoE’s Bailey, ECB’s Schnabel, and various Fed officials (Barr, Bowman).
    *   **Fed Beige Book:** Scheduled for release at 7:00 PM UK time to provide more clarity on US economic health.

**Notable Quotes**
> "The narrative coming out of the company [ASML] is that actually, we're sold out. We are supply-constrained, and we can't deliver whatever everybody wants." — **Guy Johnson, Bloomberg Host**

> "It’s still closed. The shortages are building. The longer this thing goes on for, the longer we’re going to have a problem for... it's tech versus the Strait of Hormuz at the moment." — **Guy Johnson, Bloomberg Host**

> "The dollar has given up most of its war gains... maybe [the US] is paying more of a consumer price than some other places in the world where the price at the pump is more controlled." — **Anna Edwards, Bloomberg Host**

> "This isn't just a Middle East story that stayed in the Middle East in terms of its impact on travel and therefore luxury." — **Anna Edwards, Bloomberg Host**

briefings.title: JUST IN: Secretary Of Agriculture Brooke Rollins Hosts Other Cabinet Members For Press Conference
briefings.tldr: The Trump administration marked Tax Day by highlighting the "Working Families Tax Cut Act," which delivers historic relief to middle-class Americans and rural communities, while simultaneously announcing the launch of the first-ever USDA Office of Seafood to integrate fishermen into federal agricultural support programs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The Trump administration marked Tax Day by highlighting the "Working Families Tax Cut Act," which delivers historic relief to middle-class Americans and rural communities, while simultaneously announcing the launch of the first-ever USDA Office of Seafood to integrate fishermen into federal agricultural support programs.

## Economic Relief and Tax Implementation
* **Broad Tax Savings:** The administration reported that 53 million filers have claimed at least one new tax cut, with the average refund this season exceeding $3,400.
* **Specific Provisions:**
    * **No Tax on Tips/Overtime:** Over 6 million filers claimed "no tax on tips," and 25 million claimed "no tax on overtime," resulting in average savings of $7,000 for service workers.
    * **Senior Relief:** 51 million seniors (88% of those on Social Security) will now pay no tax on their Social Security benefits.
    * **Standard Deduction:** Over 100 million filers utilized the now-permanent double standard deduction.
* **Capital Investment:** The act made permanent 100% immediate expensing for capital-intensive business investments, specifically aiding farmers and small businesses.

## Revitalizing Rural America and Agriculture
* **The "Death Tax":** Secretary Brooke Rollins confirmed the act averted the sunset of the death tax exemption, protecting two million family farms from liquidation.
* **Direct Rural Investment:**
    * **Rural Opportunity Zones:** $100 billion is being driven into rural investment through Opportunity Zones, shifting the program's focus from urban to heartland communities.
    * **Health Transformation:** $50 billion is committed to the Rural Health Transformation program, overseen by Dr. Oz.
* **Commodity Price Protection:** Reference prices for major commodities (corn, soybeans, wheat) will increase by 10% to 21%, providing up to $13 billion in additional revenue protection starting this October.
* **Trade Deficit Reduction:** The administration reported cutting the inherited $50 billion agricultural trade deficit by 40% through 18 new trade deals.

## The Historic Launch of the USDA Office of Seafood
* **"Farmers of the Sea":** Secretary Rollins announced the first-ever **USDA Office of Seafood**, officially recognizing commercial fishermen as food producers rather than just resource harvesters.
* **Integration of Services:** The office will provide fishermen access to USDA tools previously reserved for land farmers, including:
    * Risk management and insurance tools.
    * Marketing support and federal financing.
    * Disaster and weather incident relief.
* **Regulatory and Economic Protection:** 
    * **Inspection Standards:** Officials noted that currently, only 0.1% of imported seafood is inspected; the new office aims to protect domestic markets from "toxic" imported fish.
    * **Defunding Offshore Wind:** Fourth-generation lobsterman Dustin Delano praised the administration for eliminating subsidies for offshore wind projects that threaten traditional fishing grounds.

## Federal Efficiency and Regulatory Reform
* **Permitting Acceleration:** Secretary Doug Burgum highlighted a massive reduction in bureaucracy, reporting that Environmental Impact Statements (EIS) that previously took four years are now being completed in 24 days while still following the law.
* **Eliminating "Bloat":** Secretary Rollins identified several taxpayer-funded studies (e.g., studies on transgender mice and "racism in the pest business") that were defunded to refocus the USDA on core agricultural production.
* **Energy Independence and Inputs:**
    * **Fertilizer Crisis:** Secretary Rollins reported that fertilizer prices have risen 40% in the last month; the administration is engaging DOJ and fertilizer CEOs to prevent price gouging.
    * **Natural Gas Advantage:** Secretary Burgum noted that because the U.S. is a net exporter of natural gas (the primary component of nitrogen fertilizer), the administration intends to build domestic infrastructure to ensure American farmers have the world’s lowest fertilizer costs.

> "For the first time in a long time, commercial fishermen are being recognized for what we truly are: food producers... This is not just about policy; it’s about people. It’s about ensuring that the American fisherman, the farmer of the sea, has a future in this country."
— **Dustin Delano**, *Maine Lobsterman and Fisherman in Residence at NOAA*

> "We’ve taken federal employees and we’ve basically created mind-numbing, soul-sucking jobs where all they do is follow a bunch of regulations that aren’t literally something that Congress passed... When you get rid of the red tape, it not only helps the industry, it helps the federal team members."
— **Doug Burgum**, *Secretary of the Interior*

> "We have a handful of companies in the world supplying fertilizer... I will not leave this building in two years and nine months if we have not made significant progress to build out that infrastructure [in America]."
— **Brooke Rollins**, *Secretary of Agriculture*

briefings.title: Jensen Huang – Will Nvidia’s moat persist?
briefings.tldr: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argues that Nvidia’s moat is built on "accelerated computing" rather than mere chip manufacturing, leveraging a 20-year head start in the CUDA ecosystem to deliver 50x performance gains through algorithmic co-design.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argues that Nvidia’s moat is built on "accelerated computing" rather than mere chip manufacturing, leveraging a 20-year head start in the CUDA ecosystem to deliver 50x performance gains through algorithmic co-design. He warns that aggressive export controls on China risk ceding the world's second-largest market and forcing a shift toward non-American technology standards, potentially undermining long-term U.S. leadership.

## The Business of "Electrons to Tokens"
*   **Fundamental Model:** Huang defines Nvidia’s core mission as the transformation of "electrons to tokens," where the "token" (a unit of intelligence) is the new valuable molecule of the digital economy.
*   **"As Much as Needed, As Little as Possible":** Nvidia’s philosophy is to focus only on the "insanely hard" parts of the stack while partnering for everything else.
    *   **Hyperscaler Strategy:** Nvidia avoids becoming a cloud provider/hyperscaler because the market is already well-served; instead, they focus on backstopping "neoclouds" (e.g., CoreWeave, Crusoe, Nebius) to ensure their architecture remains the industry standard.
*   **The Software Explosion:** Contrary to fears that AI will commoditize software, Huang predicts the number of software instances will skyrocket as AI agents—not just humans—become the primary users of tools like Excel and Synopsys.

## Supply Chain as a Strategic Moat
*   **Capital Commitments:** Reports indicate Nvidia has between $100 billion and $250 billion in purchase commitments with foundries (TSMC) and memory suppliers (SK Hynix, Micron).
*   **Informing Upstream Investment:** Huang’s "moat" involves persuading CEOs of supply chain partners to invest in capacity (like CoWoS packaging) years in advance by demonstrating massive downstream demand.
*   **Bottleneck Resolution:**
    *   **Scaling Timeframes:** Most hardware bottlenecks (logic, memory, CoWoS) are 2-3 year problems that resolve once a clear demand signal is provided.
    *   **The Energy Constraint:** Huang identifies energy policy—not chip fabrication—as the primary long-term bottleneck for "reindustrializing" the U.S. and building AI factories.
    *   **Human Capital:** He expresses concern over "doomers" discouraging careers in software engineering or radiology, noting that AI increases the demand for experts rather than replacing them.

## Competitive Edge: CUDA vs. ASICs (TPUs)
*   **Programmability vs. Fixed Logic:** While TPUs and ASICs (Application-Specific Integrated Circuits) are optimized for matrix multiplication, Huang argues Nvidia's "accelerated computing" is superior because it is programmable.
    *   **Algorithmic Leaps:** Nvidia achieved a 50x jump from Hopper to Blackwell—far exceeding Moore’s Law—by simultaneously optimizing processors, fabric (NVLink), and libraries.
*   **TCO and Market Reach:** Huang claims Nvidia offers the best Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) and "performance-per-watt," challenging competitors like Amazon (Trainium) and Google (TPU) to prove their cost-advantage claims via public benchmarks like MLPerf.
*   **The Investment "Miss":** Huang admits a previous mistake in not realizing that early AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) required massive investment from suppliers. Nvidia is now correcting this by participating in multi-billion dollar funding rounds for major labs.

## Geopolitical Strategy and the China Debate
*   **The Danger of Conceding Markets:** Huang strongly opposes total export bans on China, arguing that conceding 40% of the world's technology market forces China to build its own ecosystem (e.g., Huawei’s record growth) and accelerates domestic chip innovation.
*   **Energy as an Offset:** While the U.S. has superior 3nm/2nm chips, Huang notes that China’s abundance of energy and manufacturing capacity allows them to compensate for using older 7nm technology by simply "ganging up" more chips.
*   **The "American Tech Stack":** He argues it is in the U.S. national interest for the world’s researchers (50% of whom are Chinese) to develop their models on American hardware and standards.
    *   **Standardization Risk:** If Chinese-developed open-source models are optimized for domestic hardware, the "American tech stack" loses its global dominance as AI diffuses to the Global South.

## Notable Quotes
> "Our job is to do as much as necessary and as little as possible to enable that transformation [electrons to tokens] to be done at incredible capabilities." — **Jensen Huang**

> "Nvidia's GPUs, accelerators, are like F1 racers. It takes quite a bit of expertise to be able to push it to the limit... we use a ton of AI to create the kernels that we have." — **Jensen Huang**

> "If we scare this country into thinking that AI is somehow a nuclear bomb... I don't know how you're helping the United States. You're doing it a disservice." — **Jensen Huang**

> "Moore's Law is dead. Between Hopper and Blackwell, from the transistors themselves, call it 75% [improvement]... Blackwell is 50 times Hopper. My point is: architecture matters. Computer science matters." — **Jensen Huang**

briefings.title: LIVE: Karoline Leavitt Holds White House Press Briefing With Bessent And Loeffler Amid Iran Talks
briefings.tldr: On Tax Day, the Trump administration highlighted record tax refunds and the success of "Working Families Tax Cuts" (notably no tax on tips/overtime), while confirming a maximum-pressure economic blockade on Iran and announcing the construction of a 250-foot "Triumphal Ark" for America’s 250th anniversary.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
On Tax Day, the Trump administration highlighted record tax refunds and the success of "Working Families Tax Cuts" (notably no tax on tips/overtime), while confirming a maximum-pressure economic blockade on Iran and announcing the construction of a 250-foot "Triumphal Ark" for America’s 250th anniversary.

## Tax Day Statistics and "Working Families" Provisions
Karoline Leavitt and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent detailed the impact of the administration's tax policies, framing them as a "promises made, promises kept" success for the middle class.

* **Filing Data:** Over 53 million filers claimed at least one signature tax cut this season.
    * The average refund for the current filing season is over **$3,400**.
    * More than 105 million filers used the permanently doubled standard deduction.
* **Signature Provisions:** 
    * **No Tax on Overtime:** Cited by Bessent as the most popular provision, used by 25 million filers with an average deduction of $3,100.
    * **No Tax on Tips:** Claimed by 6 million filers, averaging a $7,100 deduction.
    * **Senior Relief:** 30 million seniors claimed an enhanced deduction averaging $7,500.
    * **American-Made Cars:** Over 1 million filers claimed a deduction for interest on auto loans for American-made vehicles.
* **"Trump Accounts":** 5 million families have opened these child savings accounts, with 1.2 million eligible for a $1,000 "seed bonus."

## Small Business and Industrial Growth
SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler reported that the administration's tax and regulatory policies have spurred a "re-industrialization" of the U.S. economy.

* **Small Business Relief:** Approximately 12 million small businesses saw average tax savings of $7,000.
    * The 20% small business "pass-through" deduction has been made permanent to provide planning certainty.
* **Capital Access:** The SBA set an all-time lending record of **$41 billion** over the past year.
* **Manufacturing Resurgence:** Loeffler cited 100% expensing for equipment and R&D as the primary driver for "reshoring" industries and creating new factory shifts.
    * Mentioned the "Big Beautiful Building" at Blue Patriot Fab in Omaha as a direct result of tax incentives.

## Foreign Policy and Energy Markets
The briefing addressed the ongoing economic and naval strategy regarding Iran and its impact on domestic energy costs.

* **"Operation Economic Fury":** Secretary Bessent confirmed a maximum-pressure campaign, including secondary sanctions.
    * The U.S. has notified two unnamed Chinese banks that they face sanctions if they continue processing Iranian oil payments.
    * The U.S. will not renew general licenses for Russian or Iranian oil.
* **The Strait of Hormuz Blockade:** The U.S. is enforcing a full blockade on vessels entering or departing Iranian ports, though freedom of navigation remains for non-Iranian traffic.
    * **Mediation:** Leavitt confirmed that Pakistan is the "only mediator" currently facilitating talks between the U.S. and Iran.
* **Gas Price Outlook:** Bessent expressed optimism that gas prices will feature a "3" in front of them (under $4.00) between June 20 and September 20, contingent on the reopening of the Straits.

## Cabinet Updates and National Landmarks
* **Federal Reserve:** Secretary Bessent confirmed that Kevin Warsh's confirmation hearing for Fed Chair is scheduled for the 21st of this month.
* **Acting Attorney General:** Leavitt stated that Todd Blanch remains the Acting AG; no permanent personnel updates were provided despite media speculation regarding other candidates.
* **United States Triumphal Ark:** The administration will submit plans tomorrow for a 250-foot tall monument on Columbia Island in the Potomac River. 
    * The structure is intended to commemorate the 250th anniversary of American independence (Semiquincentennial).

> "If the Democrats in Congress had gotten their way and blocked President Trump’s historic legislation, Americans would have faced the largest tax hike in history—nearly $4 trillion. The average taxpayer would have seen a 22% increase in their tax rates."
— **Karoline Leavitt**

> "Iran is—or used to be—the largest state sponsor of terrorism... we have told countries that if you are buying Iranian oil, if Iranian money is sitting in your banks, we are now willing to apply secondary sanctions."
— **Scott Bessent**

> "Not a single worker, not a single small business asked to pay a dollar more in taxes. Yet, every single congressional Democrat voted to raise taxes... Thankfully, Republicans united behind the common sense policy of letting Americans keep more of what they earn."
— **Kelly Loeffler**

briefings.title: OMB Dir. Russell Vought testifies before House panel on Trump's FY 2027 budget request—4/15/26

people.name: Russell Vought
people.role: Director, Office of Management and Budget

briefings.tldr: OMB Director Russell Vought presented a FY 2027 budget proposal centered on a historic 42% increase in defense spending ($1.5 trillion) and deep non-defense cuts, while defending the administration’s controversial use of "impoundments" to withhold congressionally appropriated funds.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
OMB Director Russell Vought presented a FY 2027 budget proposal centered on a historic 42% increase in defense spending ($1.5 trillion) and deep non-defense cuts, while defending the administration’s controversial use of "impoundments" to withhold congressionally appropriated funds.

## FY 2027 Budget Priorities & Fiscal Strategy
* **Defense vs. Non-Defense:** The budget requests $1.5 trillion for defense—a "paradigm-shifting" 42% increase—balanced by a 10% cut to non-defense discretionary spending. 
* **Agency Eliminations:** Vought confirmed the administration's intent to fully shutter the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting (NPR/PBS), citing "mismanagement" and "woke programming."
* **Law Enforcement Surge:** The proposal includes a 13% increase for the Department of Justice, specifically to combat violent crime and establish a new "National Fraud Division."
* **Economic Assumptions:** The administration claims a 10% reduction in the deficit due to growth and the "Big Beautiful Bill," though the Minority cited CBO estimates suggesting the bill adds $4.7 trillion to the long-term debt.

## The Impoundment & Executive Power Conflict
* **Defending Impoundments:** Vought explicitly stated, "Of course I believe in impoundments," arguing that the President has the constitutional right to spend less than Congress provides. 
* **Disregarding Oversight:** When questioned on GAO findings that the administration illegally withheld billions for NIH and Head Start, Vought dismissed the GAO as "typically wrong" and "partisan."
* **"Fiscal Futility":** Vought characterized the administration's aggressive withholding of funds as an end to "decades of fiscal futility," asserting that the executive branch must use every "fiscal toolbox" to curb spending.

## Social Safety Net & Healthcare Reforms
* **Medicaid & Work Requirements:** The budget leans on "historic welfare reform" by implementing work requirements for able-bodied adults. 
* **Healthcare Coverage:** Ranking Member Brendan Boyle (D-PA) highlighted CBO data suggesting 15 million Americans will lose healthcare coverage; Vought countered that these individuals were "ineligible, illegal, or able-bodied adults refusing to work."
* **Elimination of Assistance Programs:** The administration proposes zeroing out the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) and the Capital Magnet Fund, labeling them "historically fraudulent" or "woke."

## Energy, Inflation, and Geopolitics
* **The "War of Choice":** Minority members criticized the $350 billion set aside for a "war of choice" with Iran, arguing it has spiked gas prices (exceeding $4.00/gallon) and drained resources from domestic programs like childcare.
* **Tariff Revenue:** Vought projected that "America First" tariffs would generate approximately $4.7 trillion in revenue, serving as a primary pillar of the administration's fiscal stabilization plan.
* **Foreign Aid Cuts:** The budget terminates various international programs, including funds for green energy in Vietnam and "gender-affirming care" in Guatemala, refocusing those dollars on the "Department of War."

## Notable Quotes
> "Fiscal futility has ended with the return of President Trump. In just one year, the Trump administration and Congress have made historic progress on righting our fiscal ship." — **Russell Vought, OMB Director**

> "A budget is a statement of our priorities... This budget sees the hungry, it sees the homeless, it sees the vulnerable, and it turns away." — **Rep. Morgan McGarvey (D-KY)**

> "The Supreme Court has never spoken on this issue [impoundment]... We believe we have the moral and legal high ground every time we make a decision." — **Russell Vought, OMB Director**

> "We are paying people not to work... Trump comes in, and in one year, secures the border, stops the flow, and pulls down the drive of our deficit." — **Rep. Jodey Arrington (R-TX), Chairman**

briefings.title: White House Press Briefing
briefings.tldr: On Tax Day, the administration highlighted the impact of the "Working Families Tax Cuts," reporting an average refund of $3,400 and significant participation in new tax exemptions for tips and overtime.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
On Tax Day, the administration highlighted the impact of the "Working Families Tax Cuts," reporting an average refund of $3,400 and significant participation in new tax exemptions for tips and overtime. Strategically, the White House is maintaining a naval blockade and "maximum pressure" sanctions on Iran, characterizing short-term energy price volatility as a necessary trade-off for global security.

## Individual Tax Relief and IRS Performance
* **Tax Cut Participation:** Approximately 53 million filers (45% of all returns) claimed at least one of the administration’s signature tax cuts.
    * **No Tax on Overtime:** Claimed by over 25 million filers, with an average deduction of $3,100.
    * **No Tax on Tips:** Utilized by over 6 million service workers, averaging a $7,100 deduction.
    * **Senior Benefits:** Over 30 million seniors utilized enhanced deductions, averaging $7,000.
* **Refund Statistics:** The average refund for the current filing season is over $3,400. The administration claims these are the largest refunds in U.S. history.
* **Withholding Strategy:** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent encouraged Americans to adjust their withholdings to receive an "automatic real wage increase" on a monthly basis rather than waiting for an annual refund.
* **Trump Accounts:** Five million families have opened these accounts for their children, with 1.2 million eligible for a $1,000 bonus. The program aims to increase national financial literacy and long-term savings.

## Small Business and Industrial Reinvestment
* **Economic Impact:** SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler reported that 12 million small businesses saved an average of $7,000 this year. 
* **Key Policy Drivers:**
    * **Pass-Through Deduction:** The 20% small business pass-through deduction is now permanent, which the SBA credits for the creation of one million new jobs.
    * **100% Expensing:** Provisions for equipment and R&D expensing are being used to "re-industrialize" the U.S. manufacturing base.
* **Small Business Optimism:** Despite a recent dip in March data, Loeffler asserted that the long-term trend remains above the 50-year average, contrasting it with 34 consecutive months of below-average optimism during the previous administration.

## Energy and International Sanctions
* **Gas Price Outlook:** Secretary Bessent projected that gas prices would return to the "$3.00 range" between June 20 and September 20. He noted that while crude oil prices have dropped recently, retail stations have been slow to lower prices.
* **Iran Blockade and Sanctions:** The U.S. is enforcing a full naval blockade on all vessels entering or departing Iranian ports. 
    * **Strategic Sacrifice:** Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt stated the administration is willing to accept "short-term volatility" in energy prices to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.
    * **Secondary Sanctions:** The Treasury has issued warnings to two Chinese banks, threatening secondary sanctions if they continue to process payments for Iranian oil.
* **Mediation:** Pakistan remains the sole mediator in ongoing negotiations with Iran; the administration denied reports that they had requested an extension of the current cease-fire.

## Justice Department and National Commemoration
* **Attorney General Transition:** Todd Blanche is currently serving as the acting Attorney General. Leavitt emphasized that the President’s top priority for the permanent role is "accountability for the weaponization of justice."
* **U.S. Triumphal Arc:** The administration announced plans to build a 250-foot tall "United States Triumphal Arc" in Washington, D.C. (Logan Circle) to commemorate the 250th anniversary of American independence. Construction is slated to begin this year.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "No tax on overtime. It is the American way. If you want to work longer hours, you can keep more money." 
— **Scott Bessent**, Treasury Secretary

> "Small business is big business. They are a massive economic engine that creates two-thirds of all new jobs... the working family tax cuts are putting money back into the pockets of the hardest working Americans." 
— **Kelly Loeffler**, SBA Administrator

> "The President has been clear: this is short-term disruption for the long-term strategic goal of the United States to ensure the world's leading state sponsor of terror cannot obtain a nuclear weapon." 
— **Karoline Leavitt**, White House Press Secretary

briefings.title: Why Cost Per Token Is the Only Metric You Need for AI TCO
briefings.tldr: The traditional focus on hardware-centric metrics like "FLOPs per dollar" fails to capture the true cost of AI; "Cost per Token" is the definitive metric for Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) because it accounts for the entire efficiency stack—from power generation and cooling to software optimization and throughput.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The traditional focus on hardware-centric metrics like "FLOPs per dollar" fails to capture the true cost of AI; "Cost per Token" is the definitive metric for Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) because it accounts for the entire efficiency stack—from power generation and cooling to software optimization and throughput.

## Redefining the Economics of AI Infrastructure
*   **The Shift from Inputs to Outputs:** Historically, data center efficiency was measured by compute cost or GPU hours. However, as AI data centers evolve into "intelligence factories," the only output that generates revenue or utility is the token.
*   **Input vs. Outcome Metrics:**
    *   **GPU Hour:** A time-based metric that ignores efficiency, power leakage, and actual work performed.
    *   **FLOPs per Dollar:** Measures raw compute potential but ignores the overhead of the surrounding facility.
    *   **Cost per Token:** A holistic metric that reveals the true margin of an AI business by factoring in both CapEx (hardware/facility) and OpEx (energy/maintenance).
*   **Generational Performance Gains:** Comparing NVIDIA Blackwell to the previous Hopper generation illustrates the metric gap: 
    *   **FLOPs per dollar** shows a ~2x improvement.
    *   **Cost per million tokens** shows a **~35x lower** cost.

## The Data Center as a "Token Factory"
*   **The Atomic Unit of Intelligence:** Tokens are the physical goods of the new industrial revolution, with electricity serving as the primary raw material. 
*   **Factory Economics:** Just as a traditional manufacturer must know the cost of every part produced to ensure profitability, AI operators must understand their cost per token. Failing to account for power leaks or low utilization results in "selling at a loss."
*   **The "Inference Iceberg":** The sticker price of a GPU is only the tip of the iceberg. Beneath the surface lie critical costs including networking, memory, cooling, and—most importantly—power delivery efficiency.
*   **Utilization Rates:** A factory sitting idle increases the cost per token. Software optimizations like disaggregated inference are essential to keep "token factories" running at maximum capacity.

## Power as the Primary Lever for Scalability
*   **Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE):** Dr. Gerro Prinsloo notes that while hyperscalers achieve ~10% overhead, inefficient data centers can reach 100% overhead (a PUE of 2.0).
    *   In a 100% overhead scenario, half of the electricity paid for never reaches the chip to produce a token.
*   **Energy Sourcing and Transportation:**
    *   **Generation:** Scaling requires a "redundancy of sources," including natural gas, nuclear, geothermal, and emerging "metal fuels."
    *   **Voltage Optimization:** Moving to 800V DC power systems reduces "leaks" during the transport of energy from the grid to the chip.
*   **The Cooling Revolution:** Shifting from air cooling to liquid-cooled, closed-loop systems (keeping hardware at ~45°C) allows for higher density and more tokens per megawatt without wasting water through evaporation.

## Escaping "Spiky" Demand: The Rise of AI Agents
*   **From Queries to Continuous Load:** Early AI usage was "spiky" (users asking single questions). With the rise of AI agents (e.g., Claude), usage is shifting to a "flat line" where models run 24/7 to complete complex tasks. 
*   **Unlimited Demand for Intelligence:** NVIDIA observes an exponential takeoff in token demand. As businesses deploy an agent for every employee, the pressure on the power grid will move from peak-load management to constant, massive demand.
*   **The Power-Compute Convergence:** For the first time in history, the utility industry and the data center industry are merging. Utility executives and AI infrastructure planners are now forced to co-design the grid to prevent a global "intelligence shortage."

## Notable Quotes
> "If you’re running the factory... and you're selling tokens at the same rate as someone else that doesn't have the same amount of losses as you do, your factory's going to go out of business." — **Dr. Gerro Prinsloo**

> "We have fundamentally an unlimited demand for intelligence as a species, and we live in a power-constrained world." — **Carter Abdallah**

> "The atomic unit of the industrial revolution was the electron; in this case, the atomic unit is the token. Tokens can be applied to a wide array of things—medicine, software, entertainment, everything." — **Carter Abdallah**

> "I think that the cost per token really is the metric that we need to talk about here. Anything else is getting lost in either something that is too far up the abstraction ladder or you're getting into the weeds of something that isn't actually the meat that drives your P&L." — **Nader Khalil**
